story.vex: Spend it all on the wrong thing. I'll wait by the gap you left open. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED before it started: the crew funds the one control that actually closes a gap Vex could use. Astro: "Now our credits go where the risk is, not where the shiniest tool is."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Three purchase proposals are on the table. Read proposals.txt, then decide each one: worth-it or skip-it, based on cost versus the loss it actually prevents.

1. type proposals.txt
2. classify <item> worth-it   OR   classify <item> skip-it
files.C:\\Citadel\\proposals.txt:
PURCHASE PROPOSALS
-------------------
proposal-relay-password   cost: 0 credits    prevents: a repeat of the exact breach Vex already used (high likelihood, high impact)
proposal-shield-diagnostic cost: 8,000 credits prevents: a rare failure that would cost 2,000 credits to fix (low likelihood, low impact)
proposal-backup-relay      cost: 400 credits   prevents: total comms blackout if the main relay fails (medium likelihood, high impact)

steps.title: Read the proposals
steps.body: Astro: "Know the numbers before you decide." `type proposals.txt`.

steps.title: Fund the gap, not the gadget
steps.body: Rivet: "Free and closes the exact breach Vex used? Fund it. Expensive and barely helps? Skip it." Classify all three: `classify proposal-relay-password worth-it`, `classify proposal-shield-diagnostic skip-it`, `classify proposal-backup-relay worth-it`.

objectives.label: proposal-relay-password: worth-it (free, closes the known gap)
proposal-shield-diagnostic: skip-it (expensive, rare and cheap to fix anyway)
proposal-backup-relay: worth-it (moderate cost, prevents a high-impact blackout)
